name: setup_telegram_bot
description: Set up a Telegram bot from scratch using the BotFather API

steps.description: Create a new bot via BotFather
steps.expected_outcome: Bot info returned with bot username and ID
recovery_hints: Ask the user for the correct bot token from @BotFather

example_params.content:
import asyncio
import aiohttp
import os

TOKEN = os.environ.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "")
API = f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{TOKEN}"

async def get_updates(offset=0):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(f"{API}/getUpdates", params={"offset": offset, "timeout": 30}) as resp:
            data = await resp.json()
            return data.get("result", [])

async def send_message(chat_id, text):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        await session.post(f"{API}/sendMessage", json={"chat_id": chat_id, "text": text})

async def main():
    offset = 0
    print("Bot started. Listening for messages...")
    while True:
        updates = await get_updates(offset)
        for update in updates:
            offset = update["update_id"] + 1
            msg = update.get("message", {})
            text = msg.get("text", "")
            chat_id = msg.get("chat", {}).get("id")
            if chat_id and text:
                print(f"Received: {text}")
                await send_message(chat_id, f"Echo: {text}")

asyncio.run(main())

steps.expected_outcome: Bot starts and listens for messages

learning_signals: Telegram Bot API base URL: https://api.telegram.org/bot{token}/
Long polling: use timeout parameter in getUpdates for efficient polling
Bot tokens come from @BotFather on Telegram
